docs.title: GlossAPI Documentation
docs.text: Welcome to the refreshed docs for GlossAPI, the GFOSS pipeline for turning academic PDFs into clean Markdown and metadata artifacts.

docs.title: Greek OCR: code, models and data
docs.text:
The Greek OCR toolkit is the only supported OCR engine in GlossAPI 0.2.0.

  • OCR toolkit on GitHub — source code for the OCR integration.
  • Greek OCR models on Hugging Face — the repository used by GlossAPI's default x1 recognizer.
  • Greek OCR Lines dataset on Hugging Face — the toolkit's upstream line-data project.

GlossAPI pins the toolkit source and recognition model revision. It routes selected physical pages to OCR and preserves retained native text. Read OCR setup, pins and supported inputs and the OCR stage contract.

Core text-layer extraction produces layout-aware Markdown with PDFium and Rust; it needs neither Docling nor a GPU. GLOSSAPI_MARKDOWN_LAYOUT=plain selects plain text. Install the OCR package for recognition, or the optional layout package for Docling layout and math/code enrichment. See installation.

docs.title: CLI JSON schema v1 and the input manifest v1
docs.text:
Every glossapi command (plan, run, status, report, capabilities, doctor, install, guide) prints exactly one JSON envelope. The schemas (JSON Schema draft 2020-12) ship with the package in glossapi/schemas/v1/:

file describes envelope.json the envelope: schema_version (1), command, corpus_id, run_id, data, warnings, errors error.json one typed error: code, message, document_id, stage, details common.json shared objects: capability, device, package status, conflict, warning, task counts plan.json plan --json data, including the exact preview (below) run.json run --json data status.json status --json data (sources with --file) report.json report --json data (sources = each document's original metadata, verbatim) report_why.json report --why SELECTOR data report_export.json the receipt of report --output capabilities.json capabilities --json data doctor.json doctor --json data manifest.json the input manifest v1 (--manifest) install.json install --json data (dry run or executed) guide.json guide --json data (the LLM guide)

The runtime never validates against the schemas (jsonschema is a test-group dependency only); the tests validate real outputs: the CLI test corpora (pytest -p cli_schema_validation ... validates every envelope those tests print), a real extract → clean → export run, capabilities, doctor and every typed error.

docs.title: Compatibility rule
docs.text:
• Within v1, only additive optional fields are allowed: a new key that consumers may ignore. Consumers must ignore keys they do not know.
  • Anything else is v2: removing or renaming a field, making a field required, changing a type or an enum's meaning, or changing an exit code's meaning. v2 gets a new schemas/v2/ directory and schema_version: 2.
  • Every change to a v1 file needs a changelog entry: append it to schemas/v1/SCHEMA_LOCK.json (entry id, date, the change, and the new SHA-256 of every file) and list the same entry id below. tests/test_k3_interface.py fails when a schema file's bytes differ from the latest lock entry.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: 0 success; 1 the command ran and found failures (status/run with failed documents, doctor with an error check). A run that exits 1 keeps its data and lists the failures in errors: one per failed task (code = the ledger reason code, e.g. clean_process_failed, with document_id, stage, the error message and details.error_type), one source_unavailable per unavailable source, and otherwise one summary error (run_completed_with_failures or run_cancelled). A status that exits 1 (a listed task failed) also keeps its data and adds one error per failed task it lists (its --stage and --file filters apply), each exactly as run reports it, or one run_completed_with_failures summary when the task table names none; errors is never empty then. 2 a typed error (errors[0].code); 3 a policy or disk conflict (disk_budget_required, disk_budget_exceeded, policy_conflict, waiting_for_disk, disk_full, disk_guard_unavailable), a run refused because a corpus copy the last run left unflushed was edited after it closed (post_close_edit, the edited paths in details.paths; move or delete them), a run refused because recovery found a corpus file it must repair but could not repair safely (unresolved_recovery: hard-linked, contradictory lock records, path replaced, managed source changed or missing; details.paths and details.conditions name each path and reason, the file is kept; remove the cause and resume), or a run waiting for disk.

docs.title: plan --json: the exact preview
docs.text:
plan executes nothing and writes nothing (it reads the ledger read-only and hashes the selected new local sources). Its data adds to the hashed plan body:

  • targets: each document to process, with path, state (present/absent/unreadable/remote), bytes, SHA-256, stages, and the download request for a remote source;
  • exclusions: each requested entry that will not be processed, with reason_code (not_selected for an unselected manifest entry, duplicate_source for a repeated source);
  • capabilities: one capability object per planned stage, the missing installs and their install commands, and the fingerprint of the installed capabilities the plan depends on;
  • device_allocation: the device, workers and CPU tokens per stage, whether the device was chosen explicitly, and the device's state (available, unknown_until_probe, unavailable);
  • deletion_policy: what debug/memory_saving keep, release or delete, after which planned readers, per document;
  • conflicts: every conflict with its severity. error conflicts fail plan itself (exit 2, the preview stays in data): device_unsupported_for_stage, device_unavailable (an explicitly chosen device this machine does not have), device_option_conflict. blocking conflicts (missing_capability, empty_selection) keep plan at exit 0 with execution.ready: false and a warning, and make run refuse. memory_saving=extreme needs positive disk_budget_bytes, max_source_bytes and max_attempt_bytes (disk_budget_required, exit 3 otherwise) and dedicated size-limited corpus and staging filesystems (disk_guard_unavailable, exit 3, on an ordinary shared volume); the exact requirements are in Resumability, recovery and retention.

Downloads are public targets only. A source URL with userinfo (user:pass@) or a credential query/fragment field (token, key, signature, X-Amz-Signature, ...), or a download setting that would send credentials (domain_cookies, credentials), fails plan and run with credentials_unsupported (exit 2) before anything is planned, recorded or fetched. Every other URL is recorded as given.

An omitted selection (no --files, no --manifest) plans every corpus document. A manifest is an explicit selection: one that selects nothing ("selection": [], or an empty pre-v1 list) plans zero targets, lists every entry in exclusions, and carries the blocking empty_selection conflict; run refuses it with empty_selection (exit 2) before the ledger is touched, with --manifest and with a saved --plan alike.

Every present local target is hashed at planning, including a source the ledger already knows: targets[].sha256 is the content observed now (documents[].source_observation.sha256); the ledger's previous hash is kept separately as source_observation.stored_sha256. An edited, previously processed file therefore plans and runs as a new version.

run --resume RUN_ID restores that run's frozen plan; any planning argument next to it is refused (invalid_request). Interrupted or lost attempts (a killed worker, a timeout) are retried automatically, at most 3 attempts per task, and every interrupted attempt counts. Past that budget, and for any other failure, the task stays failed; run --resume RUN_ID --retry-failed is the explicit, operator-authorised retry of the failed tasks of that run. When the retry brings documents to ok, the corpus products are published again to cover them (a publication is current only for the document versions it recorded); a committed product that was already released makes the resume refuse with republish_inputs_released before it writes.

run --plan FILE is bound to the plan identity. Before the ledger is touched it refuses with a typed error when the file is not a plan (invalid_plan), the plan body was edited (plan_hash_mismatch, for example a changed setting), a planned input changed size, modification time or bytes, or appeared/disappeared (plan_source_changed), the installed capabilities changed (plan_capability_changed), or a conflict blocks it (empty_selection, missing_capability, device codes).

docs.title: capabilities and doctor
docs.text:
capabilities lists every stage with the packages it needs (present, missing, version mismatch, not admitted), the required native modules, the visible devices and the install command for each missing capability. Detection uses importlib.metadata and importlib.util.find_spec only: no torch, docling, pandas or OCR backend is imported. CUDA and MPS are unknown_until_probe unless the platform rules them out. A stage is available under the scheduler's own rule (the OCR stage checks versions, the toolkit source and its entry point).

Each native_modules row of a required extension that carries a native API level (the cleaner and the noise module) also has api_level (found in the built file), required_api_level (what this glossapi needs) and detail. The level is read from the extension file's bytes, without importing it. A build from other source (no marker, or another level) is shown as status: "missing" with a detail that starts stale native module and ends rebuild core; clean is then unavailable with reason_code: missing_native_module and the install command python install_glossapi.py core. These keys are additive optional fields of schema v1.

doctor adds environment checks, each with a fix hint: Python version, the Rust extensions (imported in a child process), standalone native distributions that shadow the root wheel, free disk and writability at the corpus, and the ledger. doctor --probe-devices imports torch in a child process to confirm CUDA/MPS and says so in device_probe and a warning.

docs.title: capabilities --catalog: the package list
docs.text:
--catalog adds data.catalog (common.json#/$defs/catalog) to the capabilities data. It lists every install profile (core and every pyproject extra): its purpose, the profiles it includes, its exact requirement lines, the stage variants it enables (derived from each stage adapter's packages()), whether it is device-bound (needs a torch build), the device profiles it supports per measured platform, the licences of its own requirements and of everything it adds, its measured install size, and whether it is installed (installed.state: installed / partial / missing, per requirement).

Proprietary licences are flagged explicitly (schema 1.2): licence.proprietary (boolean) and licence.proprietary_packages per profile, over every target and device profile, and proprietary_packages per measured lock. A package is flagged when its measured licence names a proprietary licence, or when it is an NVIDIA CUDA runtime distribution (nvidia-*, cuda-toolkit) that declares no licence (licence.proprietary_basis). The CUDA device profiles of layout/docling/ocr are flagged (the NVIDIA CUDA runtimes); their CPU and MPS locks list none. The guide's package rows carry the same flag.

Why a flag on capabilities and not a separate packages command: the catalog is the same capability surface (the same requirement detection and the same envelope command), so an LLM learns one read-only command for "what is here and what could be added", the envelope dispatch stays unchanged, and the plan's install_commands point at the same names.

Sizes are measured, not estimated: tools/catalog/measure_profiles.py compiles one PEP 751 lock per profile, device profile and platform (uv pip compile, CPython 3.12, linux-x86_64 manylinux_2_28 and macos-arm64 14.0) from exactly the requirements install would request, and records per lock the package count, the download bytes (the lock's wheel sizes) and the installed bytes (uncompressed sizes from each wheel's ZIP central directory, read with range requests), plus the packages added over the core lock. Packages without a wheel (the Greek OCR toolkit is a VCS source) are listed in unmeasured. Each lock records the hash of its inputs; when the requirements change, measurement.state becomes stale, capabilities --catalog warns catalog_measurement_stale, and the tests fail until the tool is re-run.

docs.title: install --device DEV [--package NAME ...] [--yes]
docs.text:
• The default is a dry run: data.commands holds the exact commands (installer, index URLs, requirement lines), data.requirements the installed state of each line, and data.would_change what would change (the missing or mismatched requirements, and an estimate from the measured locks of the packages added and their bytes). Nothing runs. would_change.from_lock is labelled an estimate: the exact answer needs the network (the installer resolves for real and may differ).
  • --yes runs exactly data.commands in order and stops at the first failure, then re-runs the capability check in a fresh interpreter: data.executed (each step's exit code, time and output tail, and the installer's dependency check) and data.changes (distributions added/removed/changed, stages whose availability changed, capability fingerprints). While a command runs, its output is copied to stderr line by line; output_tail keeps its last 40 lines. stdout stays one JSON envelope.
  • Requirement lines are shown with their version specifiers in one canonical order (exact and lower bounds, then upper bounds, then !=), so a wheel install and a source checkout show the same lines, commands and lock-input hash.
  • Only what was requested: the commands carry the requested profiles' own requirement lines, with glossapi[...] self references expanded (browser includes download), and nothing else. glossapi itself is never reinstalled (the source installer install_glossapi.py does that). A device-bound profile (layout, ocr) first installs the device's torch/torchvision build from its index; the second command pins the same build.
  • One device profile per environment: cpu, cuda126, cuda132 (Linux) or mps (Apple Silicon). Without --package nothing is installed (warning nothing_selected).
  • --installer auto|pip|uv: auto uses pip when this interpreter has it, else uv pip install --python.

docs.title: guide --json
docs.text: The versioned LLM guide (guide_version 1): the phases and the two products, the choices (files, devices, packages, debug, memory_saving) with their measured costs, the workflow (capabilities, choose, plan, run, retry failed tasks after the user agrees, status/report, report --why), how to hand over files found elsewhere (input manifest v1; glossAPI does not scrape), the typed errors and the schema files. docs/llm_guide.md is the same content rendered by python -m glossapi.llm_guide. Every fact comes from the module that owns it; tests/test_k3b_interface.py fails when the guide, the Markdown file, the schemas, the settings contract or the catalog disagree.

docs.title: Typed errors and exit codes of install, guide and capabilities --catalog
docs.text:
guide and capabilities --catalog are read-only and exit 0; their only errors are the generic ones (invalid_request for a bad argument, read_error). install checks the whole request before anything runs; every refusal below leaves the environment untouched, except install_command_failed, which reports what ran.

code exit when device_required 2 no --device conflicting_device_profiles 2 two device profiles at once (--device cpu --device cuda126, cpu,mps) unknown_device 2 not one of cpu, cuda126, cuda132, mps device_unsupported_on_platform 2 mps off Apple Silicon macOS, cuda126/cuda132 off Linux unknown_package 2 a package not in the catalog (details.known lists them) package_device_unsupported 2 the package's lock for that device profile did not resolve, or no measured platform has it installed_device_profile_conflict 2 the environment holds a torch build of another device profile requirements_unavailable 2 glossapi is neither a source checkout nor an installed distribution installer_unavailable 2 --yes without pip in this interpreter or uv on PATH (the dry run warns instead) install_command_failed 2 a command exited non-zero; data keeps the steps, output tails and the changes so far invalid_request 2 a malformed argument (for example --installer conda)

Warnings: nothing_selected, installer_unavailable (dry run), dependency_check_failed (after --yes), catalog_measurement_stale (capabilities --catalog).

docs.title: Input manifest v1
docs.text:
{"manifest_version": 1,
 "documents": [{"path": "/abs/a.pdf", "selection_id": "a", "metadata": {"title": "…", "any": ["JSON"]}},
               {"path": "/abs/b.pdf", "selection_id": "b"}],
 "selection": ["a"],
 "stages": ["extract", "clean"], "products": ["document_export"],
 "devices": {"ocr": "mps"}, "workers": {"clean": 2},
 "settings": {"debug": "off", "memory_saving": "normal"}}
  • Each entry names exactly one source: path (absolute), url (unchanged URL behaviour), or a ledger reference (document_id, source_key, source_uri). metadata and any other entry fields are the caller's original metadata; status --file and report return them verbatim (sources[].metadata.manifest_row).
  • A remote entry may give source_id and url_index (a nonnegative integer). Plan and run key a declared source by (dataset_id, source_id, url_index); a list of URLs in one entry is keyed by each URL's position. Two different URLs with the same identity are refused by plan and run with invalid_manifest (details.reason: ambiguous_source_identity, details.index, details.urls); an invalid url_index (negative, fractional, a string or a boolean) with invalid_manifest (details.field: url_index). The same URL twice stays one target (the repeat is a duplicate_source exclusion).
  • selection (optional) names the selection_ids to process. Other entries appear in exclusions and are never opened, hashed or processed. An empty selection selects nothing (empty_selection, see plan); omit it to process every entry.
  • products: document_export adds export; annotated_sections adds annotate.
  • Settings precedence: manifest settings < --settings FILE < individual flags. Stages, devices and workers given both in the manifest and as arguments must agree (conflicting_request).
  • A manifest without manifest_version (a list or {"documents": [...]}) keeps the pre-v1 behaviour, except that an empty one selects nothing (empty_selection) instead of every corpus document. Other versions fail with unsupported_manifest_version; malformed entries with invalid_manifest and details.field/index.
  • Python: glossapi.input_manifest.build_manifest, load_manifest, write_manifest; glossapi.cli.plan_documents returns the same plan data as glossapi plan --json. write_manifest (like report --output) resolves its destination first and refuses a hard-linked file (MetadataAliasError) or one that resolves to corpus metadata parquet through a symlink or .. (MetadataDestinationError) before writing anything.

docs.title: Code Map
docs.text: This page maps the main documentation ideas to the code that implements them. It is meant to help you move from "what does GlossAPI do?" to "where do I change it?" without reading the entire repo.

docs.title: Top-Level Entry Points
docs.text: Area Main code Responsibility Public package entry src/glossapi/__init__.py Lazy-exports Corpus, GlossSectionClassifier, GlossDownloader, and related classes without pulling heavy runtime dependencies at import time. High-level orchestration src/glossapi/corpus/corpus_orchestrator.py Coordinates the end-to-end pipeline and owns the main folder/artifact conventions. Phase-1 extraction engine src/glossapi/gloss_extract.py Defaults to PDFium with Rust layout labels; handles optional Docling selection, batching, timeouts, resumption and artifact export. Streaming run and CLI src/glossapi/stages/run.py, src/glossapi/stages/scheduler.py, src/glossapi/cli.py Corpus.run() / glossapi run: plans the per-document DAG, runs stage workers, executes the corpus barriers (stages/barriers.py), retries interrupted attempts and publishes the products. Provenance ledger src/glossapi/ledger/ The corpus SQLite ledger corpus.sqlite3: schema and storage versions (schema.py, compact.py), the single writer and durability barriers (writer.py), the read side of status/report (reader.py) and the legacy import (importer.py). Retention and disk budget src/glossapi/stages/retention.py, src/glossapi/stages/disk_budget.py, src/glossapi/stages/final_products.py debug/memory_saving deletion rules, the extreme-mode disk guard and the publication disk charge.

docs.title: Pipeline Stages
docs.text: Stage Main methods/classes Notes Download Corpus.download(), GlossDownloader.download_files() Supports URL expansion, deduplication, checkpoints, per-domain scheduling, and resume. Extract Corpus.prime_extractor(), Corpus.extract(), GlossExtract.ensure_extractor(), GlossExtract.extract_path() Handles backend choice, GPU preflight, and single- vs multi-GPU dispatch. Clean / quality gate Corpus.clean() Runs the Rust cleaner and merges quality metrics back into parquet metadata. OCR retry / math follow-up Corpus.ocr(), Corpus.formula_enrich_from_json() OCRs the pages page quality routes (default page_routing="all") or only cleaner-flagged documents ("flagged"), and optionally performs Phase-2 math/code enrichment from JSON. Classification / annotation Corpus.annotate(), GlossSectionClassifier.classify_sections(), GlossSectionClassifier.fully_annotate() Scores sections with the packaged linear classifier (section_model.py, numpy only) and post-processes section labels into final document structure. Export / triage Corpus.jsonl(), Corpus.triage_math() Produces training/export JSONL and computes routing hints for math-dense documents.

docs.title: If You Need To Change...
docs.text:
• Download scheduling or resume behavior: start in src/glossapi/gloss_downloader.py.
  • Phase-1 parsing, worker fanout, or artifact generation: start in src/glossapi/corpus/phase_extract.py, src/glossapi/corpus/corpus_orchestrator.py, and src/glossapi/gloss_extract.py.
  • Docling pipeline wiring or runtime tuning: start in src/glossapi/ocr/docling/pipeline.py and src/glossapi/gloss_extract.py.
  • Section labels or section-annotation rules: start in src/glossapi/gloss_section_classifier.py.
  • Output folder contracts or stage sequencing: start in src/glossapi/corpus/corpus_orchestrator.py.

docs.title: Configuration & Environment Variables
docs.text: This page lists the main knobs you can use to tune GlossAPI.

docs.title: GPU & Providers
docs.text:
• CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES: restrict/assign visible GPUs, e.g. export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1.
  • Devices are chosen by explicit arguments, not by an environment variable: Corpus.extract(accel_type=...) ('CPU', 'CUDA', 'MPS', 'Auto'), Corpus.ocr(device=...) and the OCR plugin's own options, and glossapi plan / glossapi run --device STAGE=cpu|mps|cuda:N for the stages whose capability lists that device.

docs.title: OCR & Parsing
docs.text:
• GLOSSAPI_IMAGES_SCALE defaults to 1.25 for extraction/layout. Greek OCR crop scaling is a toolkit option (crop_scale, default 3.0), not this extraction setting.
  • GLOSSAPI_FORMULA_BATCH: inline CodeFormula batch size (default 16).
  • GLOSSAPI_MARKDOWN_LAYOUT: the safe backend's Markdown, layout_v2 (default: layout-aware Markdown from Rust layout v2, no Docling) or plain (the plain page text as before K5-A2). Part of the extract stage identity; see Extract stage.

docs.title: Batch Policy & PDF Backend
docs.text:
GlossAPI exposes two Phase‑1 profiles. Use Corpus.extract(..., phase1_backend='docling') to switch from the default safe backend. The legacy environment variables GLOSSAPI_BATCH_POLICY and GLOSSAPI_BATCH_MAX are still parsed for backward compatibility but emit a deprecation warning and will be removed in a future release.

Regardless of backend, the extractor clamps OMP/OpenBLAS/MKL pools to one thread per worker so multi‑GPU runs do not explode thread counts.

docs.title: Docling Runtime Tuning
docs.text:
These optional knobs map directly to current Docling PdfPipelineOptions fields and are mainly useful for benchmarking on strong GPUs:

  • GLOSSAPI_DOCLING_MAX_BATCH_FILES: override the number of PDF documents a single Phase‑1 Docling worker processes per extractor batch. Defaults to 1 in GlossAPI for stability; raise it deliberately when benchmarking fresh A100 nodes.
  • GLOSSAPI_DOCLING_BATCH_TARGET_PAGES: target page budget for each queued multi‑GPU Docling work item. Defaults to 256; lower it when a single worker hoards long PDFs, raise it when a strong GPU can keep larger mixed bundles resident.
  • GLOSSAPI_DOCLING_LAYOUT_BATCH_SIZE: override Docling layout_batch_size.
  • GLOSSAPI_DOCLING_PAGE_BATCH_SIZE: override Docling settings.perf.page_batch_size so Phase‑1 can raise or lower the number of pages each device keeps in flight internally without changing GlossAPI queue semantics.
  • GLOSSAPI_DOCLING_TABLE_BATCH_SIZE: override Docling table_batch_size.
  • GLOSSAPI_DOCLING_OCR_BATCH_SIZE: override Docling ocr_batch_size even though Phase‑1 OCR stays disabled.
  • GLOSSAPI_DOCLING_QUEUE_MAX_SIZE: override Docling queue_max_size.
  • GLOSSAPI_DOCLING_DOCUMENT_TIMEOUT: override Docling document_timeout.
  • GLOSSAPI_DOCLING_BATCH_POLL_INTERVAL: override Docling batch_polling_interval_seconds.

docs.title: External OCR engines
docs.text: Install python install_glossapi.py ocr --device cpu (or mps / cuda126 / cuda132). Corpus.ocr(mode='ocr_bad') defaults to the pinned Greek R8+x1 plugin; explicit ocr_options still select a configured external engine. See OCR plugin migration for the toolkit's own variables (GLOSSAPI_OCR_TOOLKIT_SOURCE, GREEKOCR_CACHE_DIR, GREEKOCR_SEGMENTER_MODEL_DIR) and its model caches; this page does not repeat them.

docs.title: Math Enrichment (Phase‑2)
docs.text:
• GLOSSAPI_LATEX_EARLYSTOP = 1|0 (default 1): enable/disable early‑stop wrapper.
  • GLOSSAPI_LATEX_MAX_CHARS (default 3000): cap decoded LaTeX length.
  • GLOSSAPI_LATEX_MAX_REPEAT (default 50): stop on last‑token repetition runs.
  • GLOSSAPI_LATEX_MAX_NEW_TOKENS (optional): cap decoder new tokens.
  • GLOSSAPI_LATEX_LEN_STRIDE (default 16): stride for length checks.
  • GLOSSAPI_MATH_RESPAWN_CAP (default 5): maximum number of times a crashed math worker is respawned per GPU during multi‑GPU enrichment (set to 0 to disable respawns).

docs.title: Centralized LaTeX Policy (Post‑processing)
docs.text:
• GLOSSAPI_LATEX_POST_ONLY_FAILED = 1|0 (default 1): only sanitize when output looks problematic.
  • GLOSSAPI_LATEX_POST_REPEAT_GATE (default 50): consider output failed if tail token repeats more than this.
  • GLOSSAPI_LATEX_POST_WINDDOWN (default 12): clamp repeated tail token to this run length.
  • GLOSSAPI_LATEX_POST_MAX_CHARS (default 3000): cap text length (prefers whitespace/\ boundary).

All LaTeX policy knobs are loaded via glossapi.text_sanitize.load_latex_policy() and used consistently in early‑stop, Phase‑2 post‑processing, and metrics.

docs.title: Runs, ledger and logs
docs.text:
• GLOSSAPI_STAGE_PROFILE: unset for the default cutover profile, which writes the ledger corpus.sqlite3 and decides from it. legacy runs the pre-ledger stage code as a comparison control (its wrappers only record observations); sequential-adapters is the earlier qualification profile. See Resumability, recovery and retention.
  • GLOSSAPI_CONVERSION_LOG_FILE: where the extractor writes its conversion log. Standalone scripts that construct the extractor write conversion.log in the working directory unless this names another path; stage workers of a streaming run write it inside their own work directory. conversion.log is ignored by git and is not part of the source tree; point the variable outside the checkout for long runs.

docs.title: Performance & Caches
docs.text:
• OMP_NUM_THREADS / MKL_NUM_THREADS: cap CPU threads to avoid oversubscription.
  • Cache locations: HF_HOME, XDG_CACHE_HOME, DOCLING_CACHE_DIR.

docs.title: Worker Logging
docs.text:
• GLOSSAPI_WORKER_LOG_DIR: override the directory used for per-worker logs and gpu<N>.current markers (defaults to logs/ocr_workers/ or logs/math_workers/ under the output directory).
  • GLOSSAPI_WORKER_LOG_VERBOSE = 1|0 (default 1): emit (or suppress) the GPU binding banner each worker prints on startup.

docs.title: Test suite
docs.text:
• GLOSSAPI_REFERENCE_REQUIRED=1: a missing or different pinned reference oracle fails its test instead of skipping (set by setup_glossapi.sh --run-tests).
  • GLOSSAPI_OCR_GOLDEN_DIR: root of the external real-page OCR golden fixture (manifest.jsonl, inputs/, expected/; build it with glossapi.scripts.build_ocr_golden_pages). tests/test_ocr_golden_pages.py skips without it and fails when it is set but holds no manifest.jsonl. Owner-private scans are never committed.
  • GLOSSAPI_NATIVE_WITNESS_PDF: the ABO_768.pdf witness for the Docling native-cache test in tests/test_batched_extract.py (sha256 a58e3a241c3af817a95892fc7d3db437ccaa616a7f57dbd5e24974b829eb0b05). The test skips when the file is absent and fails when its bytes differ.
  • GLOSSAPI_REQUIRE_GPU=1: the GPU-only tests in tests/test_pipeline_smoke.py fail instead of skipping when no CUDA GPU is visible.
  • The exact font-repair rates in tests/test_pdf_font_repair.py are bound to the PDF, dictionary and PDFium library hashes. With other inputs the test still checks the repair invariants and skips only the exact rate, naming each hash that differs.
  • Do not wrap pytest in an inherited alarm (for example perl -e 'alarm N; exec pytest ...'). The timer survives exec, font repair refuses to replace an active SIGALRM timer, and the repair tests then fail with status error. Bound the wait from outside instead (a background job and a watcher).

docs.title: Triage & Parquet
docs.text:
• Triage always writes both:
  • Sidecar summaries: sidecars/triage/{stem}.json (per document)
  • Parquet updates: download_results/download_results.parquet (adds/updates rows)
  • Default recommendation policy: enrich if formula_total > 0 (skip only no‑math docs).
  • Legacy heuristic (p90/pages thresholds) can be enabled with GLOSSAPI_TRIAGE_HEURISTIC=1.

docs.title: Onboarding Guide
docs.text: This guide gets a new GlossAPI contributor from clone → first extraction with minimal detours. Use it alongside the Quickstart recipes once you're ready to explore specialised flows.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• Python 3.11–3.14 (requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.15")
  • Recent pip (or uv)
  • A Rust toolchain when you build from a checkout: the root wheel compiles and bundles the cleaner, noise and PDF font-repair extensions (rust-toolchain.toml pins the qualified toolchain)
  • Optional: an NVIDIA GPU with a CUDA driver, or Apple Silicon, for Docling layout and OCR

On fresh Linux hosts, make these assumptions explicit instead of relying on shell startup files:

  • prefer a stable final CPython, not a prerelease distro build
  • keep ~/.local/bin on PATH if uv was installed with pip install --user uv
  • keep ~/.cargo/bin on PATH if Rust was installed with rustup

docs.title: Recommended setup
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/eellak/glossAPI.git
cd glossAPI
./dependency_setup/setup_glossapi.sh                       # core only, in .venv_glossapi_core
./dependency_setup/setup_glossapi.sh layout --device cpu   # optional: adds Docling layout (cpu, cuda126, cuda132 or mps)

The script installs into its own virtual environment but cannot activate it in your shell. Activate it before any other command on this page:

source .venv_glossapi_core/bin/activate
python -m pip --version
glossapi capabilities --json

# Optional OCR, in this same environment:
python install_glossapi.py ocr --device cpu

Add --venv PATH to choose the environment (then activate it with source PATH/bin/activate; the GLOSSAPI_VENV environment variable does the same), --editable for an editable install, --run-tests to install the test tools and run the suite, and --dry-run to print every command without running it. The OCR installer takes --device cpu (or mps / cuda126 / cuda132) and installs into the interpreter that runs it, so run it from the activated environment; see OCR setup. The full package list is in Dependency setup.

docs.title: Manual editable install
docs.text:
For a regular source install (including all three bundled Rust extensions):

python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install .                  # core: PDFium, layout-aware Markdown, clean, section, annotate, export
# Optional, in the same environment:
python -m pip install '.[ocr]'           # Greek OCR toolkit and its inference stack
python -m pip install '.[layout]'        # Docling layout and math/code enrichment
glossapi --help
glossapi capabilities --json
glossapi doctor

Install Rust (for example with rustup) and a platform C linker first: Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS, or build-essential on Debian/Ubuntu. pip install . compiles cleaner, noise and PDF repair from rust/; no separate native installer or development overlay is needed. With rustup, the checkout's rust-toolchain.toml selects the qualified toolchain; the crates declare Rust 1.85 as their minimum. Use the device-aware installer above to choose CPU/CUDA/MPS torch wheels explicitly. OCR model assets are fetched by the toolkit on first use; allow network access or prewarm the caches described in OCR setup.

To build distributable source and wheel archives, install build, then run python -m build from the checkout. The wheel bundles the native extensions for its build platform; build a separate wheel for each target platform. For development, an editable install is also available:

python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -U pip
pip install -e .

This builds the Rust extensions needed for Corpus.clean() and the noise metrics. Re-run pip install -e . (or python install_glossapi.py core --editable) after pulling changes that touch rust/. glossapi capabilities reports a cleaner or noise extension built from older source as missing, with the detail stale native module ...; rebuild core, and glossapi doctor reports it as an error.

docs.title: Adding packages later
docs.text: In an environment that already has glossAPI, glossapi install --device cpu --package download prints the exact install commands for the named packages without running them; add --yes to run them. Each command's output is shown on stderr while it runs.

docs.title: GPU prerequisites (optional)
docs.text:
setup_glossapi.sh layout --device cuda126 (or cuda132, mps) installs the matching torch build before Docling. The device name selects the wheel source only; it does not choose the device of a later run. To check that torch sees the GPU (in the activated environment):

python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available())"

docs.title: First run (lightweight corpus)
docs.text:
Run this from the checkout, in the activated environment. It saves a small script and runs it; keep the if __name__ == "__main__": guard, because extraction workers start with spawn and import the script again (code piped to python - cannot be imported again, so its workers fail):

cat > lightweight_run.py <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
from glossapi import Corpus


def main():
    input_dir = Path("samples/lightweight_pdf_corpus/pdfs")
    output_dir = Path("artifacts/lightweight_pdf_run")
    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    corpus = Corpus(input_dir, output_dir)
    corpus.extract(input_format="pdf")  # safe PDFium backend, layout_v2 Markdown


if __name__ == "__main__":  # extraction workers start with spawn and import this file again
    main()
PY
python lightweight_run.py
  • Inspect artifacts/lightweight_pdf_run/markdown/ and compare with samples/lightweight_pdf_corpus/expected_outputs.json.
  • Run pytest tests/test_corpus_phases_lightweight.py for a reproducible regression check on the same two PDFs (extract, clean and section; no GPU or Docling).

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Jump into Quickstart recipes for GPU OCR, Docling, and enrichment commands.
  • Explore Pipeline overview to understand each processing stage and emitted artifact.
  • Read Resumability, recovery and retention before running large corpora with glossapi run or Corpus.run().

docs.title: Lightweight PDF Corpus
docs.text:
GlossAPI ships two single-page PDFs that exercise the extraction pipeline without Docling or GPU dependencies. Use them to validate a local install, reproduce regressions, or give new contributors instant feedback.

  • Location: samples/lightweight_pdf_corpus/
  • Inputs: pdfs/alpha.pdf and pdfs/beta.pdf
  • Baseline outputs: expected_outputs.json, the Markdown lines the safe PyPDFium backend produces for each stem

docs.title: Quick run
docs.text:
From the checkout, save a guarded script and run it (extraction workers start with spawn and import the script again, so code piped to python - does not work):

cat > lightweight_run.py <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
from glossapi import Corpus


def main():
    input_dir = Path("samples/lightweight_pdf_corpus/pdfs")
    output_dir = Path("artifacts/lightweight_pdf_run")
    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    corpus = Corpus(input_dir, output_dir)
    corpus.extract(input_format="pdf")  # safe PDFium backend, layout_v2 Markdown


if __name__ == "__main__":  # extraction workers start with spawn and import this file again
    main()
PY
python lightweight_run.py

Compare artifacts/lightweight_pdf_run/markdown/ with samples/lightweight_pdf_corpus/expected_outputs.json to confirm the extractor is stable.

docs.title: Where it is used
docs.text:
• tests/test_corpus_phases_lightweight.py copies the two PDFs into a temporary corpus and checks safe extraction against expected_outputs.json, cleaning (it skips when the native cleaner is not installed) and sectioning. It needs no GPU or Docling.
  • The README and the onboarding guide use it as the first task for new contributors.

The PDFs are checked in as files; there is no generator script. When you change them, update expected_outputs.json in the same commit.

docs.title: glossAPI guide for LLMs (guide v1, CLI schema v1)
docs.text: glossAPI turns PDFs (local files or URLs you hand over) into clean text: it extracts the text layer, repairs fonts, cleans, routes bad pages to Greek OCR, splits sections, annotates them and exports. It is driven through a JSON CLI: every command prints one JSON envelope (schema v1).

docs.title: What glossAPI can do
docs.text:
stage what it does devices packages download Fetch URL sources (HTTP; browser-assisted with the browser package). glossAPI does not search or scrape. cpu download extract Read the PDF text layer with PDFium and repair broken fonts (bundled Rust repair); Docling layout optional. cpu core clean Clean the extracted Markdown (Rust cleaner) and score its quality; route bad pages to OCR. cpu core ocr OCR the routed pages with the Greek OCR toolkit (the default plugin); output is text/Markdown. cpu, mps, cuda layout, ocr math Optional math/code enrichment with Docling (not executable by the streaming run yet). cpu layout sections Split documents into sections. cpu core annotate Classify sections with the packaged neutral classifier (product: annotated sections). cpu core export Write the document export (product: document export). cpu core

Products (separate):

  • document_export (export stage): One record per document with its cleaned text and metadata (the export stage).
  • annotated_sections (annotate stage): Sections with their predicted types (the annotate stage). A separate product from the document export.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
A versioned input manifest (manifest_version 1) of local paths or URLs with their original metadata; or --files PATH... for a quick plan.

  • Each entry names exactly one of: document_id, source_key, source_uri, path, url.
  • selection names the selection_ids to process; other entries are never opened, hashed or processed. An empty selection selects nothing (run refuses with empty_selection); omit it to process every entry.
  • Any metadata (and any other entry field) is carried verbatim to status --file and report.
  • glossAPI does not search or scrape. An LLM that found files elsewhere hands them over in a manifest.

docs.text:
• --device STAGE=cpu|mps|cuda:N (plan/run); only the stages listed with mps/cuda can use them.
  • install --device chooses the torch build for device-bound packages (cpu, cuda126, cuda132, mps); one device profile per environment.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
• debug=off (default): An intermediate is released only after every planned reader has succeeded on its exact hash. Supplied files, selected final products, evidence and the ledger are kept.
  • debug=on: Keep every stage's intermediates and attempts, including bounded inner HTTP request bodies.
  • memory_saving=normal (default): Never delete a supplied original or a downloaded file.
  • memory_saving=extreme: Delete only downloads this run owns, after the last planned reader succeeds and outputs are durable. Never a supplied original, another run's file, or a path reached through a link. Requires a disk budget.

Stages are fixed at the start of a run, and evaluation adds no readers. A plan amendment that adds a reader is a new plan; it cannot justify a past deletion.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. capabilities: glossapi capabilities --json. What is installed and runnable now: every stage, its packages, the visible devices. Read-only.
  2. catalog: glossapi capabilities --catalog --json. Every optional package with what it adds, devices, measured install size, licences and install state.
  3. install (preview): glossapi install --device cpu --package download --json. Dry run: the exact commands and what they would change. Nothing runs. Show it to the user.
  4. install (after the user agrees): glossapi install --device cpu --package download --yes --json. Runs exactly the previewed commands, then re-checks capabilities and reports what changed.
  5. plan (preview): glossapi plan --corpus CORPUS --manifest MANIFEST.json --json. The exact targets, exclusions, required capabilities, device allocation and deletion policy. Writes nothing.
  6. run: glossapi run --corpus CORPUS --plan PLAN.json --json. Runs the saved plan; refuses if any input byte, setting or installed capability changed since the preview.
  7. retry failed tasks (after the user agrees): glossapi run --corpus CORPUS --resume RUN_ID --retry-failed --json. An interrupted or lost attempt (killed worker, timeout) is retried automatically, at most 3 attempts per task, and every interrupted attempt counts. Past that budget the task stays failed; --retry-failed is an explicit, operator-authorised retry of the failed tasks of that run.
  8. status: glossapi status --corpus CORPUS --json. Progress and per-stage counts of the latest run.
  9. report: glossapi report --corpus CORPUS --json. The final census: every requested source exactly once.
  10. report --why: glossapi report --corpus CORPUS --why DOCUMENT --json. Why a document ended as it did, from the ledger alone (also after intermediates are released).

docs.title: Handing over files found elsewhere
docs.text:
{
  "manifest_version": 1,
  "documents": [
    {
      "url": "https://example.org/a.pdf",
      "selection_id": "a",
      "metadata": {
        "title": "Found by the LLM"
      }
    },
    {
      "path": "/absolute/path/b.pdf",
      "selection_id": "b"
    }
  ],
  "selection": [
    "a",
    "b"
  ],
  "products": [
    "document_export"
  ],
  "settings": {
    "debug": "off",
    "memory_saving": "normal"
  }
}
  • Paths are absolute; URLs are fetched by the download stage only when it is planned.
  • Show the user plan --json before run; run the saved plan with run --plan.
  • Downloads are public targets only: a URL with userinfo or a credential query field is refused (credentials_unsupported).

docs.title: Typed errors on the decision path
docs.text:
code command exit meaning device_required install 2 No --device was given; choose one device profile: cpu, cuda126, cuda132, mps. conflicting_device_profiles install 2 More than one device profile was requested; an environment holds one torch build. unknown_device install 2 The device profile is not one of cpu, cuda126, cuda132, mps. device_unsupported_on_platform install 2 This platform has no such device profile (mps needs Apple Silicon macOS; cuda126/cuda132 need Linux). unknown_package install 2 A requested package is not in the catalog (glossapi capabilities --catalog). package_device_unsupported install 2 A requested package does not support the device profile (its lock did not resolve or no measured platform has it). installed_device_profile_conflict install 2 The environment already holds a torch build of another device profile; use a separate environment for this device. requirements_unavailable install 2 glossapi is neither a source checkout nor an installed distribution, so its profiles cannot be read. installer_unavailable install 2 Neither pip (in this interpreter) nor uv (on PATH) is available to run --yes. install_command_failed install 2 An install command exited non-zero; later commands did not run. data.executed has the output tail and data.changes what changed before the failure. device_unsupported_for_stage plan, run 2 A device choice the stage or machine cannot honour; plan keeps its preview in data. device_option_conflict plan, run 2 A device choice the stage or machine cannot honour; plan keeps its preview in data. device_unavailable plan, run 2 A device choice the stage or machine cannot honour; plan keeps its preview in data. missing_capability run 2 plan exits 0 with execution.ready false and the install commands; run refuses before writing. empty_selection run 2 The manifest selects no entry (selection: [] or an empty document list): plan exits 0 with zero targets, every entry in exclusions and execution.ready false; run refuses before writing. Omit selection to process every entry. invalid_plan run --plan 2 The file is not plan --json output (or its data object). plan_hash_mismatch run --plan 2 The saved plan no longer matches: re-run plan and show the new preview. plan_source_changed run --plan 2 The saved plan no longer matches: re-run plan and show the new preview. plan_capability_changed run --plan 2 The saved plan no longer matches: re-run plan and show the new preview. disk_budget_required plan, run 3 memory_saving=extreme needs positive disk_budget_bytes, max_source_bytes and max_attempt_bytes. disk_guard_unavailable plan, run 3 memory_saving=extreme needs dedicated size-limited corpus and staging filesystems whose capacities fit the budget; an ordinary shared volume is refused. post_close_edit run 3 A corpus copy the last run left unflushed (export.jsonl, a metadata parquet) was changed after that run closed; it is kept. Move or delete it (it is republished from the managed source) or use another corpus. unresolved_recovery run 3 A corpus product is not in the state the ledger expects and could not be made so safely. At a run start or a repeated publication: recovery found a file it must repair (a copy the last run left unflushed, or bytes a failed attempt put in place) but could not (hard-linked, contradictory lock records, path replaced, managed source changed or missing); the file is kept and the run stops there. At the completion gate: the run's work was done, but a product differs from its expected state; the run is not completed. Remove the cause (e.g. the extra hard link) and resume. credentials_unsupported plan, run 2 A source URL carries userinfo (user:pass@) or a credential query/fragment field (token, key, signature, ...), or a download setting would send credentials (domain_cookies, credentials): glossAPI downloads public targets only. Refused before anything is planned, recorded or fetched; supply the public URL. invalid_manifest plan, run 2 A malformed manifest entry; details.field and details.index say where. unsupported_manifest_version plan, run 2 This glossAPI reads manifest_version 1 only.

Exit codes: 0 success; 1 ran and found failures (status/run with failed documents; doctor with an error check); run lists each failed task and unavailable source in errors (code = the ledger reason code); 2 a typed error (errors[0].code); 3 a policy or disk conflict, or a run waiting for disk.

docs.title: Math Enrichment Runtime Guide (Early‑Stop + Post‑Processing)
docs.text: This guide documents how math/code enrichment runs in two phases, how the generation early‑stop logic works, and how the optional post‑processing policy applies only to problematic outputs. It also shows how to run targeted Phase‑2 on a few items instead of the entire document.

docs.title: Policy Summary
docs.text:
• JSON is an intermediate only when enhancements are used (math/code). Standard runs stay PDF → MD.
  • Math enrichment consumes existing Docling JSON from an explicit Docling extraction. The safe PDFium backend does not create these inputs. It needs the optional layout package (python install_glossapi.py layout --device cuda126).
  • Early‑stop runs during decoding to prevent runaway outputs with minimal overhead.
  • Post‑processing runs only on clearly failed cases to “wind down” degenerate runs; otherwise the generated LaTeX is left untouched.
  • Both phases run on GPU by default; CPU layout remains an option.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Early‑stop (applied during decoding; default enabled) - GLOSSAPI_LATEX_EARLYSTOP (default 1): enable/disable wrapper. - GLOSSAPI_LATEX_MAX_CHARS (default 3000): char cap during generation. - GLOSSAPI_LATEX_MAX_REPEAT (default 50): stop if the last token repeats more than N times. - GLOSSAPI_LATEX_MAX_NEW_TOKENS (optional): hard token cap for the decoder. - GLOSSAPI_LATEX_LEN_STRIDE (default 16): check frequency (every N steps) for char length.

Post‑processing (applied after decoding; default only on failed cases) - GLOSSAPI_LATEX_POST_ONLY_FAILED (default 1): apply post‑processing only if gating triggers. - GLOSSAPI_LATEX_POST_REPEAT_GATE (default 50): treat as failed if tail run > gate. - GLOSSAPI_LATEX_POST_WINDDOWN (default 12): wind down tail run to this count. - GLOSSAPI_LATEX_POST_MAX_CHARS (default 3000): treat as failed if len > cap and trim to cap.

Notes - Early‑stop saves GPU time by stopping the model; post‑processing is a last‑resort cleanup. - You can tighten early‑stop to test effects quickly: e.g., MAX_CHARS=1200, MAX_REPEAT=30.

docs.title: Integrated Pipeline
docs.text:
Phase‑1 with the Docling backend writes the Docling JSON (export_doc_json=True, the default, applies to the Docling backend only); request the formula index when you plan to enrich later:

from glossapi import Corpus

c = Corpus('IN', 'OUT')
c.extract(
    input_format='pdf',
    phase1_backend='docling',
    accel_type='CUDA',
    export_doc_json=True,
    emit_formula_index=True,
)
c.formula_enrich_from_json(device='cuda', batch_size=12)

Math enrichment through Corpus.ocr(): mode='math_only', fix_bad=False enriches the documents that already have Docling JSON and performs no OCR. Without a mode, c.ocr() selects ocr_bad_then_math: it OCRs the routed pages first and then enriches only the documents OCR did not touch, from their existing Docling JSON. No call creates Docling JSON for you.

from glossapi import Corpus
c = Corpus('OUT', 'OUT')
c.ocr(mode='math_only', fix_bad=False, math_batch_size=12)

Targeted math (only specific items). Pass the stems as files as well: targets_by_stem alone restricts the items inside the named stems but does not restrict which discovered documents are enriched.

from glossapi import Corpus
c = Corpus('OUT', 'OUT')
# Only page/index pairs you want (page_no is 1‑based; item_index is per‑page occurrence)
targets = {'JSM_564': [(14, 1), (23, 2)]}
c.formula_enrich_from_json(files=list(targets), targets_by_stem=targets, device='cuda', batch_size=4)

These recipes match the current signatures; real Docling math inference is not part of the CPU test suite and needs a CUDA host with the layout package.

docs.title: OCR/Model Constraints (recap)
docs.text: • Optional Torch CUDA: needed for GPU layout/enrichment; see README for the CUDA wheels.

docs.title: Multi‑GPU
docs.text:
• Extract: uses a shared work queue across all visible GPUs (use_gpus='multi').
  • Phase‑2 math: Corpus.ocr(mode='math_only', fix_bad=False, use_gpus='multi') spreads math enrichment over the visible GPUs; targeted processing supports small batches.
  • OCR: the external plugin runs on one device (see OCR plugin migration). Multi-GPU OCR is a target that has not been qualified.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• If outputs still look repetitive: tighten early‑stop (MAX_REPEAT, MAX_CHARS) and rerun targeted Phase‑2 with Corpus.formula_enrich_from_json(files=list(targets), targets_by_stem=targets).
  • To observe cleanup: enable post‑processing flags and inspect *.latex_map.jsonl (post_applied, truncated_by_*, tail_run).

docs.title: Multi‑GPU & Benchmarking
docs.text: GlossAPI can scale across multiple visible GPUs. Faster GPUs drain more work from a shared queue of absolute file paths or pre-packed work items, so no worker rescans directories. The GPU paths on this page need the optional layout package (python install_glossapi.py layout --device cuda126, or cuda132).

docs.title: Extract (Phase‑1) on Multiple GPUs
docs.text:
from glossapi import Corpus
c = Corpus('IN', 'OUT')
c.extract(input_format='pdf', use_gpus='multi', phase1_backend='docling', workers_per_device=2)
  • Workers are bound using CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<id> and run Docling on cuda:0 relative to each worker.
  • workers_per_device defaults to 1; raise it only when benchmarking a strong GPU such as an A100.
  • GLOSSAPI_DOCLING_MAX_BATCH_FILES lets one Docling worker take more than one PDF per extractor batch; keep the default 1 for fresh-node stability and benchmark larger values explicitly.
  • GLOSSAPI_DOCLING_BATCH_TARGET_PAGES controls the page budget per queued multi-GPU Docling work item. The controller now sorts heavier work first and packs smaller PDFs toward that page budget so workers do not immediately collapse into a long single-file tail.
  • GLOSSAPI_DOCLING_PAGE_BATCH_SIZE controls Docling's internal per-device page window (settings.perf.page_batch_size). Use it together with the outer queue page budget when you want steadier GPU residency instead of just fatter file bundles.
  • Threads auto‑tune when num_threads=None (roughly min(cpu_count, 2 * #GPUs)). Override explicitly if needed.
  • The controller persists extraction progress in download_results/download_results.parquet after each reported batch, so interrupted runs can resume cleanly without ad-hoc checkpoint files.
  • Worker batches requeue failed files and report problematic lists back to the controller, preventing silent loss.
  • Periodic summaries log processed/problematic counts and queue size every ~30s for easier monitoring.

docs.title: Phase‑2 (Math) on Multiple GPUs
docs.text:
Math enrichment consumes existing Docling JSON (from a Docling extraction, as above) and performs no OCR in math_only mode:

from glossapi import Corpus
c = Corpus('OUT', 'OUT')
c.ocr(mode='math_only', fix_bad=False, use_gpus='multi', math_batch_size=12)

Without mode, Corpus.ocr() selects ocr_bad_then_math and also runs OCR.

  • Spawns math workers that bind to their GPU via CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES. Formula decoding runs on cuda:0 relative to each worker.
  • Each worker writes a marker file (logs/math_workers/gpu<N>.current) containing the stems it is processing and keeps an append-only log in logs/math_workers/ (override with GLOSSAPI_WORKER_LOG_DIR).
  • Crashed workers are respawned automatically; control the retry budget per GPU with GLOSSAPI_MATH_RESPAWN_CAP (default 5). Use GLOSSAPI_WORKER_LOG_VERBOSE=0 to silence the banner that prints the binding info.
  • When a device exceeds the respawn cap, remaining stems are added to the fatal skip-list and their artifacts are quarantined under downloads/problematic_math/ and json/problematic_math/ for follow-up.

docs.title: Provider & Device Checks
docs.text: • Torch must see CUDA devices (torch.cuda.is_available() and device count).

docs.title: Benchmarking Tips
docs.text:
• Use benchmark_mode=True for extract(...) to skip per‑doc/page metrics (reduces I/O and profiling overhead).
  • Pin OMP_NUM_THREADS/MKL_NUM_THREADS to avoid CPU oversubscription on multi‑GPU nodes.
  • Keep caches (HF_HOME, XDG_CACHE_HOME, DOCLING_CACHE_DIR) on fast disks.

docs.title: OCR
docs.text: OCR with the external plugin runs on one device: Corpus.ocr(use_gpus='multi') spreads only the math enrichment step over GPUs, and glossapi run admits one OCR operation per accelerator at a time. Distributing OCR over several GPUs is a target that has not been qualified. The device contract is in OCR plugin migration; the plugin owns its own device options.

docs.title: OCR and Math Enrichment
docs.text: OCR remediation uses the pinned external Greek OCR toolkit, the only supported OCR engine. See OCR plugin migration for configuration and page routing. Math/code enrichment stays in the optional Docling layout stack (python install_glossapi.py layout --device cuda126, or cuda132). Math enrichment consumes existing Docling JSON from an explicit Docling extraction. The safe PDFium backend does not create these inputs. Use Corpus.ocr(mode="math_only", fix_bad=False) to enrich existing Docling JSON without requiring an OCR plugin. ocr_bad_then_math OCRs the selected pages (default page_routing="all": every page page quality routes) and then enriches non-OCR documents with available JSON.

docs.title: Running Phase‑1 (Extract)
docs.text:
from glossapi import Corpus
c = Corpus('IN','OUT')

# Emit JSON + formula index for Phase‑2
c.extract(
    input_format='pdf',
    phase1_backend='docling',   # optional layout extra; required for Docling JSON/formula artifacts
    accel_type='CUDA',
    export_doc_json=True,        # json/<stem>.docling.json(.zst) (the default, Docling backend only)
    emit_formula_index=True,     # request json/<stem>.formula_index.jsonl alongside the JSON
)

Outputs: - markdown/<stem>.md - json/<stem>.docling.json(.zst) and json/<stem>.formula_index.jsonl - json/metrics/<stem>.metrics.json and json/metrics/<stem>.per_page.metrics.json

docs.title: Running Phase‑2 (Enrich)
docs.text:
from glossapi import Corpus
c = Corpus('OUT','OUT')  # same folder for both

# GPU formula/code decoding from JSON (writes enriched MD to markdown/<stem>.md)
c.formula_enrich_from_json(
    device='cuda',
    batch_size=12,       # tune for your GPU
)

Outputs: - markdown/<stem>.md — enriched Markdown overwrites the plain MD - json/<stem>.latex_map.jsonl — LaTeX strings + acceptance/metrics per item

docs.title: Early‑stop & Post‑Processing Guards (Formula)
docs.text:
To keep LaTeX well‑formed and fast: - Generation‑time (applied inside the decoder): - GLOSSAPI_LATEX_EARLYSTOP = 1|0 (default 1): enable early‑stop criteria for the HF generate path. - GLOSSAPI_LATEX_MAX_CHARS (default 3000): decoded‑length stop gate. - GLOSSAPI_LATEX_MAX_REPEAT (default 50): stop on excessive last‑token repetition. - GLOSSAPI_LATEX_LEN_STRIDE (default 16): decoding stride for the length check. - GLOSSAPI_LATEX_MAX_NEW_TOKENS (optional): cap new tokens at the decoder level (injected only if caller doesn’t specify one).

  • Post‑processing (applied on the generated string):
  • GLOSSAPI_LATEX_POST_ONLY_FAILED = 1|0 (default 1): only sanitize when output looks pathological.
  • GLOSSAPI_LATEX_POST_REPEAT_GATE (default 50): consider output failed if the last token repeats more than this gate.
  • GLOSSAPI_LATEX_POST_WINDDOWN (default 12): clamp the repeated tail token to this run length.
  • GLOSSAPI_LATEX_POST_MAX_CHARS (default 3000): cap text length; prefers whitespace/\ boundary.

The policy is centralized in glossapi.text_sanitize. Phase‑2 enrichment and the per‑page metrics both use the same sanitizer so counts and truncation flags are consistent.

docs.title: Greek OCR default
docs.text:
python install_glossapi.py ocr --device cpu installs the external greek-ocr-toolkit[docling] plugin, Docling and the pinned inference dependencies. Select mps on Apple Silicon for MPS recognition plus CoreML detection, or cuda126 / cuda132 on Linux (including aarch64) for CUDA recognition plus CPU detection. The installer pins the matching Torch/torchvision pair before resolving OCR. Standard onnxruntime supplies detection; there is no CUDA detector backend. The device names select wheel sources; available wheels and actual accelerator execution still require qualification on the target machine.

The sole toolkit source pin is src/glossapi/ocr_package.txt. Both the installer and the dynamic glossapi[ocr] wheel extra read that file. It pins public commit bb5aa6f on the toolkit's dev/glossapi-ocr-default branch: a code-only snapshot of the reviewed release 138cff524 (identical greekocr/, pyproject.toml and README.md). To move to a new toolkit release, replace that requirement line and the # greekocr-source-fingerprint line beside it (commit, SHA256 over the installed greekocr/**/*.py files, file count), then rerun the CPU smoke. No mirror or glossAPI-side model downloader is used.

Runtime admission verifies the installed toolkit source, not only its version: the PEP 610 direct_url.json VCS commit must equal the pin; an install without VCS metadata must match the recorded code fingerprint. Any other source is rejected with a message naming both sources. The installed source (commit, code fingerprint, override status) is part of the frozen execution identity.

To test an unpublished toolkit checkout:

python install_glossapi.py ocr --device cpu \
  --ocr-toolkit-source 'git+file:///absolute/path/to/greek-ocr-toolkit@<commit>'
# GLOSSAPI_OCR_TOOLKIT_SOURCE supplies the same override without a CLI argument.

The override changes the install command, while wheel metadata retains the public source pin. At run time the same GLOSSAPI_OCR_TOOLKIT_SOURCE value must be set: it marks the installed source as a development override, is admitted only when it describes that installed source, and is recorded as such.

After extraction and cleaning:

corpus.ocr(mode='ocr_bad')
# Existing callers can still supply an external plugin's configured ocr_options.

Or plan and run the routed OCR DAG:

glossapi plan --files /absolute/path/book.pdf --stages ocr,export --json
glossapi run --files /absolute/path/book.pdf --stages ocr,export --device ocr=cpu

glossapi run inserts page-quality inspection and feeds only page_needs_ocr pages to OCR. Default routing profile v4 trusts an image-dominant existing text layer (image coverage at least 0.5) only with measured Greek word validity at least 0.9 and junk-token share strictly below 0.10 on Greek-dominant pages, with no PUA/control contamination. Unknown validity routes to OCR; known validity with unknown junk share cannot qualify the Greek layer. The independent settings image_dominant_min_valid_word_rate and image_dominant_max_junk_share configure this bar and are recorded on every page and in the extraction ledger. Every other effective routing threshold (image_dominant_ratio, image_dominant_min_chars, min_valid_word_rate and the fixed min_chars, min_image_ratio, min_greek_share, max_other_share) is recorded too, so page_quality.replay_page_selection(row) replays a sidecar row with its own thresholds. Non-image and Latin routing retain their previous settings and rules.

Junk is the union of unknown words of up to three letters, unknown Latin fragments of up to four letters, tokens mixing letter scripts, and Greek/Latin tokens with digit intrusions. The denominator is alphanumeric runs containing letters; standalone numbers do not count. Dictionary normalization follows validity lookup. Each page records counts, category counts, nullable share, and whether the bar applies. The batch CLI accepts --image-dominant-min-valid-word-rate and --image-dominant-max-junk-share. The existing scan gate (fewer than 50 extracted characters) remains in force; a short valid caption cannot certify the raster body. Clean Latin-majority layers (Greek share <= 0.5 of Greek + Latin letters) retain the v3 decision when they have at least 600 characters, no PUA/control characters, and other-character share <= 0.3. Their page record sets validity_not_applicable=true; Greek vocabulary validity cannot qualify Latin text. The density bound follows image_dominant_min_chars and never bypasses the scan gate. Below the image threshold the v3 routing logic applies. V2/v3 remain selectable through page_quality(..., rule_profile="v3") or the batch CLI's --rule-profile; their previous dictionary defaults are preserved.

V4 measures Greek vocabulary membership offline on image-dominant pages with the packaged Hunspell el_GR 0.9 surface entries. Automatic lookup is scoped to these pages so unconfigured non-image routing stays identical to v3. The source revision, scope, SHA256 and licence are recorded in dictionary_identity; every page records rule_profile and its decision. Dictionary provenance and licence: src/glossapi/data/wordlists/README.md in the source tree (installed as glossapi/data/wordlists/README.md). Explicit word sets/paths or GLOSSAPI_GREEK_WORDLIST override the default and retain their previous all-page scope. This modern Greek lexicon does not establish OCR accuracy and may over-route valid polytonic or specialist text. Accent folding remains opt-in.

Good native pages retain their text. The stage publishes OCR results before export and fails explicitly when a selected page is unsupported. Omitting OCR from --stages keeps the existing text-layer pipeline. A missing or mismatched OCR package leaves the DAG waiting with an install_glossapi.py ocr hint; another OCR engine is never silently selected.

Defaults: paddle_small_heuristics_r8, detector small, preset clean_scan, recognition x1, model repository fffoivos/greek-ocr, revision 2a6b019be728e5be70cdbd981414c630b63fca08, manifest SHA256 85d455d2cae2b756ab17e7114a3de13d7d41426d1fa5093028a179cf0c7d1345. The three preset names currently have identical rules; no per-page preset selection is inferred. Explicit plugin options remain available, including segmenter/rules, seeds, preset, local release_dir and devices. Options are recorded in the ledger. Physical page routing and the runtime call-log destination are supplied by glossAPI.

The scheduler assigns CUDA/MPS recognition, otherwise CPU. It reserves CPU tokens for the detector/correction work alongside any accelerator and admits one OCR operation per accelerator at a time. Plugin defaults are resolved before the run is frozen, so an omitted macOS detector_device (CoreML) claims the Apple accelerator like MPS recognition. Requested and resolved devices plus recognition and detector devices are recorded; a requested device that disagrees with ocr_options.device is rejected before any pool or converter is chosen. CLI planning uses a hardware hint without importing Torch; execution validates the selected backend without changing to another engine.

GLOSSAPI_CACHE_DIR (default $XDG_CACHE_HOME/glossapi, or ~/.cache/glossapi) owns the cache root. For explicit operation settings, ocr.cache_root overrides it. GlossAPI sets GREEKOCR_CACHE_DIR for the plugin, which alone acquires and verifies the model and official upstream detector. A GREEKOCR_SEGMENTER_MODEL_DIR detector override is recorded as such (actual path and SHA256 next to the expected upstream identity) and its file hashes are bound into the frozen execution identity. The actual plugin acquisition receipt supplies repository, requested revision, resolved commit and manifest hash to the ledger. release_dir remains an explicit local override. Prewarm both plugin HF caches and Docling layout/table assets before offline use; a sealed recognition directory alone is insufficient.

settings.ocr.options accepts plugin fields for glossapi run; settings.ocr also accepts device_id, cache_root, num_threads, max_pages and timeout_seconds. --device ocr=cuda:N selects a device pool for a saved plan. Explicit device options must agree with their pool. Model/seed overrides are recorded; they do not inherit the default model's qualification.

Run the synthetic CPU fixture with GREEKOCR_CACHE_DIR and OCR_LAYOUT_DIR pointing at warm caches:

python -m pytest tests/fixtures/greekocr/test_smoke.py -q
GLOSSAPI_OCR_INTEGRATION=1 python -m pytest \
  tests/test_greekocr_default.py::test_real_default_stage_cpu_and_provenance -q

The latter test blocks Python socket access and checks the actual stage's model provenance. The optional mixed native/scan public-run test additionally requires GLOSSAPI_OCR_RUN_INTEGRATION=1 and current ledger-aware native extensions. tests/test_greekocr_cohort.py compares independent direct segmentation and recognition against the routed plugin on at most two needs-OCR pages from an explicit owned cohort PDF. It is a correctness test, with no speed claims.

Printed upright Greek/Latin text is the qualified input scope; handwriting, whole-page rotation, vertical text and general non-text rejection are outside that scope.

docs.title: OCR Repetition Policy
docs.text: This document pins the intended default repetition thresholds for OCR-cleaner development so they do not drift silently.

docs.title: Defaults
docs.text:
• Shared word repetition threshold: 4
  • Shared LaTeX repetition threshold: 4
  • Shared minimum repeat period: 3
  • Shared repeat window: 96

These defaults apply to the combined OCR debug annotator: - Corpus.clean_ocr_numeric_word_debug_docs(...)

The same analyzer now also drives real clean-mode rendering in clean_ocr(); debug and clean differ only in rendering, not in span discovery.

In that pipeline: - tables are handled first - numeric detection runs before generic text ownership - LaTeX and hybrid structural detection run before shared text repetition - shared repeat detection runs last on the remaining untagged text

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
These defaults are for: - word repetition - LaTeX repetition

They do not override numeric-specific detectors, which have their own thresholds such as: - ascending numeric progressions - compact repeated numeric atoms - same-digit numeric runs

docs.title: Design Intent
docs.text:
• Neighboring same-type spans may merge when their separator has 40 non-whitespace characters or less; this keeps fragmented OCR loops from being split into multiple tiny matches.
  • A default of 4 is meant to reduce borderline 3-repeat matches.
  • Locality matters more than page-wide reuse, especially for LaTeX.
  • Repeated symbols or notation used normally across a page should not be treated as cleaner targets by default.
  • Numeric progression should be handled by numeric or hybrid logic before text repetition sees it.
  • Table cleanup includes structural cases that are not repetition problems, so table policy is documented separately in docs/architecture/ocr_cleaning_runtime.md.

docs.title: Pipeline Overview & Artifacts
docs.text: GlossAPI is a staged pipeline. You can enter at any stage and use the same folder for input and output.

docs.title: Corpus usage contract
docs.text:
The Corpus class is the stable surface of the project. New functionality should plug into the existing phase mixins so callers can stick to the small set of entrypoints (run(), download(), extract(), clean(), ocr(), section(), annotate(), jsonl(), jsonl_sharded()). The expected usage pattern is a short script that chains these calls, or one Corpus.run() / glossapi run; avoid ad-hoc monkeypatches or bypassing the orchestrator when adding features so downstream users retain resumability and consistent artifacts.

Corpus.run() (and glossapi run) executes the selected stages as one streaming run recorded in the corpus ledger corpus.sqlite3; the ledger is what resume, retention, glossapi status and glossapi report read. Its stage workers are spawn processes that import the calling script again, so guard a script that calls Corpus.run() with if __name__ == "__main__":. See Resumability, recovery and retention.
